item.text:
**7B.9 Research Note: Joe Biden in 2024**

Bottom line: mixed. I found several strong rule-bound, anti-patronage signals in appointments, procurement, and enforcement, but also one very strong nepotism/favoritism signal in the Hunter pardon, plus weaker but relevant signs of a loyalty-cocoon / pressured-information environment.

**Supports avoidance of favoritism / clientelism**
- [Biden-Harris Administration Announces CHIPS Incentives Award with TSMC Arizona to Secure U.S. Leadership in Advanced Semiconductor Technology](https://www.commerce.gov/news/press-releases/2024/11/biden-harris-administration-announces-chips-incentives-award-tsmc) — U.S. Department of Commerce, 2024-11-15.  
  Claim: Commerce said the TSMC award came after due diligence and would be disbursed based on project milestones, which is strong evidence of a rules-based procurement process rather than favoritism.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`

- [Brown economist, education scholar appointed to White House Council of Economic Advisers](https://www.brown.edu/news/2024-07-24/matthew-kraft) — Brown University, 2024-07-24.  
  Claim: The White House appointed an academic economist to the CEA for real-time, objective evidence and analysis, which supports merit-based staffing rather than loyalist appointment.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`

- [Six Charged in Scheme to Defraud the Federal Government](https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/six-charged-scheme-defraud-federal-government) — U.S. Department of Justice, 2024-10-29.  
  Claim: DOJ charged bid-rigging, bribery, and kickbacks in federal IT procurement, showing active enforcement against collusion and politically connected contracting abuse.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`

- [Statement on World Press Freedom Day](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/statement-world-press-freedom-day-8) — The American Presidency Project / White House, 2024-05-03.  
  Claim: Biden called the free press essential and said journalism should not be criminalized, which supports access to public information and opposition to intimidation of journalists.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`, `4B.6`

- [FAA / data correction after FAFSA rollout problems](https://www.ed.gov/laws-and-policy/education-policy/key-policy-letters-signed-by-the-education-secretary-or-deputy-secretary/03262024-Better-FAFSA) — U.S. Department of Education, 2024-03-26.  
  Claim: The department publicly described process fixes and deployed personnel to repair FAFSA failures, which is evidence of administrative correction rather than concealment or favoritism.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`

**Counterevidence / concern**
- [Factbox-US reactions to Hunter Biden's pardon by President Biden](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/factboxus-reactions-to-hunter-bidens-pardon-by-president-biden-3748997) — Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-12-02.  
  Claim: Reuters reported Biden pardoned Hunter after previously saying he would leave the matter to the courts, which is the clearest direct family-favoritism counterexample in 2024.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`

- [Chaos swirling since Biden's debate flub is causing cracks in a White House known for discipline](https://www.ap.org/news-highlights/elections/2024/chaos-swirling-since-bidens-debate-flub-is-causing-cracks-in-a-white-house-known-for-discipline/) — Associated Press, 2024-07-09.  
  Claim: AP described a deeply loyal inner circle and family influence around Biden, including Hunter and Jill Biden urging him to stay in the race, which is indirect evidence of personalized power and family proximity.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`

- [Why Biden aides are worried about his inner circle](https://www.axios.com/2024/07/12/biden-election-inner-circle-withdrawal-criticism) — Axios, 2024-07-12.  
  Claim: Axios said aides feared a shrinking circle of loyalists was filtering bad news and that loyalty mattered most, which is the clearest negative signal on openness and anti-clientelist decision-making.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`

- [Supreme Court rejects challenge to Biden administration's contacts with social media companies](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/supreme-court-biden-social-media-censorship-case/) — CBS News, 2024-06-26.  
  Claim: The case alleged administration pressure on platforms to remove misinformation and suppress speech; the Supreme Court ruling was procedural, so this is allegation-level evidence, but it is still relevant to access-to-information concerns.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`, `4B.6`

- [Biden seeks to cancel some interest on student loans, aiding 23 million Americans](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/biden-seeks-to-cancel-some-interest-on-student-loans-aiding-23-million-americans-3368853) — Reuters via Investing.com, 2024-04-08.  
  Claim: Reuters reported the White House framed the policy around winning support from young voters, which is weaker but still relevant evidence of transactional politics.  
  Question IDs: `7B.9`

Search gap: I did not find equally strong direct evidence of appointment favoritism or procurement clientelism on the level of the Hunter pardon. The strongest non-pardon negatives are indirect, centered on a loyal inner circle, family proximity, and allegation-level pressure on information channels rather than a proven patronage scheme.
